rulings: CF-ONE-SALE-ONE-ADDRESS (2026-09-05): one sale resident under two cardId partitions is a split pool AND a double count. Never a delete - RETIRE marks flaggedWrong, and it is reversible.

THE KEEPER NAMES THE TWIN (2026-09-06): these twins are not rival PARSES, so neither the title predicate nor the canonical-copy rule decides them. The keeper carries `rekeyedFrom` -- the re-key's own record of the address it moved OFF -- and that address is the twin. Provenance, not inference.

The keeper was verified PRESENT in sold_comps before this list was written (per-id cross-partition probe, 2026-09-06): every entry's keeper is alive at `retireSupersededBy` carrying the run's own `rekeyedAt`. The lane reads only `fromCardId`, so `retireSupersededBy` is stamped onto the retired row as `dedupSupersededBy` and is the audit trail back to the keeper.

SCOPE: the 14 rows are every `read-back differs from the written row` failure in the 32-slot rematch-sold-comps IMPROVE fleet (2026-09-05 05:22Z - 2026-09-06 02:38Z) that a probe found resident TWICE. 21 rows reported that error; 7 are resident once and are NOT listed - a failure is not a twin until the container says so.
The other 60 fleet failures report `read-back found nothing`, a DIFFERENT class (the keeper was never found at all). They are out of scope here and are not listed.
